title: SpanGuard concurrent final-clone drops can lose the end callback
behavior: Two concurrent cloned-guard drops can both see strong_count == 2 and return before releasing their local Arc. The subsequent releases destroy SpanEnd with neither path invoking on_end. The span end/export is lost.
interleaving: A takes self.inner into its local Arc; B's clone is still alive.
A reads strong_count=2 and selects early return before its local Arc is dropped.
B takes its Arc, reads strong_count=2, and also selects early return before A releases.
A and B release their locals; SpanEnd is destroyed without its stored FnOnce callback being called.
assumptions: Separate guard clones are dropped concurrently on different threads.
No external wrapper serializes all such drops.
Sequential drops ordinarily invoke the callback on the final guard; the issue is not asserted for every drop.
parity_relation: Separate Rust implementation defect in a capability to preserve; not evidence that the TypeScript activity dashboard already exists in Rust.
upstream_provenance: Confirmed in local Git at upstream bigfish1913/pi-rust v0.6.1 / 0fb2d893206981527b14e86d68e3ddbdf2c8189a, crates/rpi-telemetry/src/context.rs:83-103; introducing blame 91d89082dd6d09d3cdbbb0d55ceb6ab88e1a9523 is an ancestor. Evidence: rust-defect-provenance.json. Not caused by the local rebrand.

review.author: /root
review.review_conclusion: Confirmed by independent source inspection; the finish Mutex does not serialize the refcount check/release and SpanEnd has no Drop implementation.

remediation_note: For an implementation follow-up, once-only finalization should live in the shared state destructor or another synchronization mechanism; application source was not changed.
